title: Charts
text: phw_sec_axis() returns secondary axis second measure. $rescale() function maps measure onto scale first axis. Wrap second measure $rescale() give object sec.axis. Colouring secondary axis match series helps readers see axis belongs .  log axis, say scale = "log" use scale_y_log10():
code: wk <- tibble(week = 1:104) |>   mutate(cases = rpois(n(), 30 + 400 * exp(-((week - 20) / 8)^2) + 250 * exp(-((week - 72) / 10)^2)),          positivity = pmax(1, 3 + 24 * exp(-((week - 22) / 9)^2) + 16 * exp(-((week - 74) / 11)^2) +                              rnorm(n(), 0, 1))) orange <- phw_col("orange")  sec <- phw_sec_axis(wk$cases, wk$positivity, name = "Positivity (%)") ggplot(wk, aes(week)) +   geom_col(aes(y = cases), fill = phw_col("navy"), width = 0.85) +   geom_line(aes(y = sec$rescale(positivity)), colour = orange, linewidth = 1) +   scale_y_continuous("Cases", sec.axis = sec) +   labs(title = "Cases and positivity by week", x = "Week") +   theme_phw(axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = orange),             axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = orange)) sec <- phw_sec_axis(wk$cases, wk$positivity, name = "Positivity (%)", scale = "log") ggplot(wk, aes(week)) +   geom_line(aes(y = cases), colour = phw_col("navy")) +   geom_line(aes(y = sec$rescale(positivity)), colour = orange) +   scale_y_log10("Cases", sec.axis = sec) +   labs(title = "The same measures on log axes", x = "Week") +   theme_phw(axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = orange),             axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = orange))

Use sep = " | " single line. phw_date() formats date dd/mm/yyyy, words style = "long", format() string. phw_number() phw_percent() return labelling functions axes. take arguments scales::label_number() scales::label_percent().
code: phw_caption("Example data", date = as.Date("2026-11-03")) #> [1] "Source: Example data\nData correct as of 03/11/2026" phw_caption("Example data", date = as.Date("2026-11-03"),             source_prefix = "Data: ", date_prefix = "As of ", sep = " | ") #> [1] "Data: Example data | As of 03/11/2026" phw_date(as.Date("2026-11-03")) #> [1] "03/11/2026" phw_date(as.Date("2026-11-03"), "long") #> [1] "3 November 2026" phw_number()(c(1200, 45000, 1250000)) #> [1] "1,200"     "45,000"    "1,250,000" phw_percent()(c(0.052, 0.4, 0.875)) #> [1] "5.2%"  "40.0%" "87.5%" age_totals <- cases |>   count(age_group) |>   mutate(cases = n * 100, share = n / sum(n)) a1 <- ggplot(age_totals, aes(age_group, cases)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = phw_number()) +   labs(title = "Cases", x = NULL, y = NULL) a2 <- ggplot(age_totals, aes(age_group, share)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = phw_percent(accuracy = 1)) +   labs(title = "Share of cases", x = NULL, y = NULL) phw_arrange(a1, a2, source = "Example data")

text: Put phwstyle format YAML header, knit usual: start working example RStudio, choose File > New File > R Markdown > Template > PHW report. knits three formats. formats call use_phw_ggplot() use_phw_flextable() knitting, don’t repeat document. Add theme_phw() PHW scale plot change something plot. Options go format name. format takes arguments R Markdown format builds , ones : toc number_sections add table contents numbered headings. title: Maps and boundaries
text: phw_map() joins data Welsh boundaries draws styled map one call. Give data, column area codes (), column colour (fill) boundary level. Areas row data grey. boundary attribution becomes caption unless set labs(). Made-values real areas look convincing neighbours similar values. helper gives area value changes smoothly across Wales, hot spot noise. makes numbers examples. maps use data.
code: set.seed(1) made_up_rate <- function(level, lo = 20, hi = 80) {   b <- phw_boundaries(level)   xy <- sf::st_coordinates(suppressWarnings(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(b))))   x <- (xy[, 1] - min(xy[, 1])) / diff(range(xy[, 1]))   y <- (xy[, 2] - min(xy[, 2])) / diff(range(xy[, 2]))   s <- 0.5 * y + 0.2 * (1 - x) + 0.5 * exp(-((x - 0.8)^2 + (y - 0.15)^2) / 0.08)   s <- (s - min(s)) / diff(range(s))   tibble(code = b$code, rate = round(lo + (hi - lo) * s + rnorm(nrow(b), 0, 3), 1)) } la <- made_up_rate("local_authority")

text: data data frame one row per unit (area, practice...). numerator, denominator Columns events population (patients, tests...), unquoted dplyr. Strings work . Rows missing value denominator 0 left , message. label Optional column unit names; units outside outer limits labelled. type "proportion" (e.g. uptake) "rate" (e.g. incidence). multiplier Scale y axis: 100 percentage, 1e5 rate per 100,000. target target value multiplied scale. title: Grouped table with nested row and column groups — phw_group_table
text: data data frame. rows Row grouping columns, outermost first, chosen dplyr::select(), e.g. c(group, type). number levels. Strings work . cols Optional column grouping columns, outermost first, e.g. year c(year, quarter). Outer levels become headers spanning columns. value Optional numeric column summarise. Without , rows counted. fun Function applied value within cell. Defaults sum (value can hold counts aggregated data). Use e.g. function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE) statistics; group total rows computed records group, adding rows . cell records 0 sum, blank max mean, give number records. NaN Inf fun blank . totals row totals show. : "group": group row shows total group (e.g. Group shows total group ), every level groups inside. "subgroup": block innermost category summed across groups (e.g. Type 1, Type 2, Type 3). "table": one total row whole table. Use character() "none" totals. total_position Put table total subgroup block "bottom" "top" table. subtotal_position Show group totals group's heading row ("header"), leave heading blank add total row group (""). col_totals column totals show cols given: "table" (one total column) "group" (total column outermost column group, cols two levels). percent Add percentages counts: "parent" (share group , e.g. Type 1 share Group ), "column" (share column total), "row" (share row total) "none". counts sums. layout "indent" puts row labels one column, indented level. "columns" gives level column, group's label sits column groups inside shifted right. separate separate outermost groups: "space", "line", "" "none". highlight Shade outermost group rows? labels Named list display names grouping columns. value_label Heading value column cols. label_header Heading label column "indent" layout. Defaults row variable labels joined " / ". total_label Label total rows columns. subtotal_label Label group totals group, {group} replaced group name. subgroup_label Heading "subgroup" block, {variable} replaced label innermost row variable, given labels. missing Label missing grouping values, NULL drop . drop Leave categories records group? digits Decimal places percentages non-integer values. renderers use unless give digits.

title: Secondary axis for a second measure — phw_sec_axis
text: primary, secondary values main axis secondary axis, just range c(min, max). stacked columns give range stack totals, e.g. c(0, 500). name Title secondary axis. scale Scale main axis: "linear" "log". sec_scale Scale secondary axis. Defaults scale. zero Line zero axes? default two linear axes, charts columns need. FALSE stretches range secondary range primary instead, uses whole panel. Log axes zero, always line two ranges. breaks, labels, guide Passed ggplot2::sec_axis(), e.g. labels = phw_percent().

title: Secondary axis for a second measure — phw_sec_axis
text: returns ordinary ggplot2::sec_axis() one extra function, $rescale(). Use together: wrap second measure $rescale() inside aes() give object sec.axis scale axis Set scale match scale add : "linear" ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(), "log" ggplot2::scale_y_log10(). log axis two measures lined log scale, axes show log-spaced breaks. secondary axis can also use different scale main one. scale = "linear", sec_scale = "log" puts log axis right linear chart, scale = "log", sec_scale = "linear" reverse. Two axes one chart easy misread, two series cross depends axes lined . Name axes, consider colouring secondary axis match series (see examples).

title: Secondary axis for a second measure — phw_sec_axis
code: library(ggplot2) d <- data.frame(week = 1:20) d$cases <- round(180 * exp(-((d$week - 9) / 4)^2) + 4) d$positivity <- 2 + 28 * exp(-((d$week - 10) / 5)^2)  # Linear: columns for counts, a line for the second measure. sec <- phw_sec_axis(d$cases, d$positivity, name = "Positivity (%)") ggplot(d, aes(week)) +   geom_col(aes(y = cases), fill = phw_col("navy")) +   geom_line(aes(y = sec$rescale(positivity)), colour = phw_col("orange"), linewidth = 1) +   scale_y_continuous("Cases", sec.axis = sec) +   theme_phw(axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = phw_col("orange")),             axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = phw_col("orange")))   # Log: the same idea on a log axis. sec <- phw_sec_axis(d$cases, d$positivity, name = "Positivity (%)", scale = "log") ggplot(d, aes(week)) +   geom_line(aes(y = cases), colour = phw_col("navy")) +   geom_line(aes(y = sec$rescale(positivity)), colour = phw_col("orange")) +   scale_y_log10("Cases", sec.axis = sec) +   theme_phw()

text: base_size Base font size points. Reports use 11 body text. base_family Font family. Defaults phw_font() (Ubuntu). ... theme settings, passed ggplot2::theme(). override PHW defaults, need separate + theme(). grid major gridlines draw: "y" (default, horizontal lines vertical bars time series), "x" (horizontal bars), "xy" "none". legend Legend position: "bottom", "top", "right", "left", "inside" "none", numeric c(x, y) inside panel. legend_title Show legend title? PHW reports usually . strip Facet strip style: "light" (grey band, navy text), "navy" (navy band, white text) "plain" (text ). axis_line Draw mid-grey line along bottom axis (left axis grid = "x")? drawn grid = "none". axis_ticks Draw axis tick marks? grid_minor Draw minor gridlines (axes grid)? title_colour, text_colour Colours title text. background Plot background. Use "transparent" slides web pages background. base_line_size, base_rect_size Line border widths, ggplot2::theme_grey(). accessible Larger text thicker lines public-facing low-vision outputs. Raises base_size least 13 makes lines points bigger. (ggplot2 4.0 lines points grow set use_phw_ggplot().) change colours: colour-blind safe palette see phw_default_palette().
